obligations: The canonical full French text is referenced by action ID, never duplicated.
The short cue is a COPY proposal, not an observed priest stage and not automatically a trigger.
Multi-stage summaries cannot activate all sub-events together or inherit the paragraph scroll position.
Form-dependent actors may be the deacon at Solemn Mass; the server has a separate clock.
A 1962 source citation and English translation do not imply independent French editorial approval.
User postures and priest icons must not be derived directly from these rubric drafts.
No text can enter live Missal, Simple or LIVE without separate source/form, reader and publication signoff.
GUIDE_ONLY entries are not single-step cues; PRIEST_MULTI_STAGE_EDITORIAL requires a separately attested stage ID before any timed display.
FOCUS_WORDS_NO_DUPLICATE protects the two Consecrations; do not overlay repeated caption on prominent Latin words.
SERVER_RIBBON_ONLY never inherits PRIEST action ownership. PRIEST_RIBBON_STATE_ONLY never becomes an instant repeated icon.
INDEPENDENT_STAGE_EDITORIAL_ONLY is used for consecration genuflection/elevation; no activation until distinct witnessed source stages are resolved.
Guide drafts describe observable rites and legitimate variants directly; do not substitute implementation commentary for the rubric itself.
Final guide prose states the rite; source-cue and implementation limitations are preserved as editorial metadata rather than intrusive commentary.
The short French draft is read at preview time from the canonical R62 French owner; no second editable French short text exists in this bilingual registry.
If the canonical French source or its approval status is missing, the entire bilingual packet must fail closed rather than substitute an outdated local copy.
R62.044: guide-only while the donor coelésti vs the parallel 1962 cælesti spelling and exact cross-sign offset remain unresolved; do not fire the Sign of the Cross at omni benedictione.

shortDraft.en: He raises his hands, lifts then lowers his eyes, joins his hands and bows profoundly.

guideDraft.en: At the altar's centre the priest extends and slightly raises his hands, lifts his eyes to God and immediately lowers them. He joins his hands, places them on the altar and, bowing profoundly, begins the Canon in a low voice.

shortDraft.en: He kisses the altar, straightens, then joins his hands.

guideDraft.en: He kisses the centre of the altar, straightens and joins his hands before his chest.

shortDraft.en: He makes three crosses over the Host and chalice.

guideDraft.en: With his right hand he makes three Signs of the Cross over the Host and chalice together, at the corresponding three phrases.

shortDraft.en: With hands extended, he commemorates the Pope and local Ordinary according to the prescribed conditions and formulas.

guideDraft.en: With hands extended, the priest commemorates the Pope unless the Apostolic See is vacant, then the diocesan Ordinary as prescribed. When the Ordinary has died, or when Mass is celebrated in Rome, the Ordinary's name is omitted. A bishop celebrating uses the appointed self-formula, while the Pope celebrating uses the special formula for the Supreme Pontiff.

shortDraft.en: At Memento, he joins and raises his hands with his head slightly bowed.

guideDraft.en: At Memento he joins his hands and raises them before his face or chest, his head slightly inclined.

shortDraft.en: He silently commemorates the living.

guideDraft.en: He pauses to remember the living. Names may be spoken quietly, but they are not obligatory.

shortDraft.en: He resumes with hands extended.

guideDraft.en: After the commemoration he resumes the prayer with hands extended.

shortDraft.en: He recites Communicantes with hands extended, using the prescribed proper form on certain days.

guideDraft.en: The priest recites Communicantes with hands extended, using the particular form prescribed for the liturgical day when one is appointed.

shortDraft.en: At the name of Jesus Christ, he bows his head.

guideDraft.en: At the name of Jesus Christ he bows his head towards the altar cross.

shortDraft.en: At Per eundem, he joins his hands.

guideDraft.en: At Per eundem he joins his hands before his chest.

shortDraft.en: He keeps his open hands over the Host and chalice until Per Christum.

guideDraft.en: At Hanc igitur he extends both hands, palms open towards the Host and chalice, maintaining them over the offerings until Per Christum. Particular forms of Hanc igitur depend on the selected Mass.

shortDraft.en: At Per Christum, he joins his hands.

guideDraft.en: At Per Christum he joins his hands before continuing.

shortDraft.en: At benedictam, adscriptam and ratam, he makes three crosses over the Host and chalice.

guideDraft.en: At benedictam, adscriptam and ratam he makes three separate Signs of the Cross over the Host and chalice.

shortDraft.en: At Corpus, he crosses the Host.

guideDraft.en: At Corpus he makes one Sign of the Cross over the Host only.

shortDraft.en: At Sanguis, he crosses the chalice.

guideDraft.en: At Sanguis he makes one Sign of the Cross over the chalice only.

shortDraft.en: He raises and joins his hands, then bows his head towards the cross.

guideDraft.en: He raises and then joins his hands, inclining his head towards the altar cross.

shortDraft.en: If other Hosts are to be consecrated, he first uncovers their vessel; then, at accepit panem, takes the Host.

guideDraft.en: At Qui pridie he continues quietly. If other Hosts are to be consecrated in a covered chalice or vessel, he first uncovers it with his right hand. At accepit panem, he takes the Host between the thumbs and index fingers of both hands.

shortDraft.en: He looks heavenward, then lowers his eyes.

guideDraft.en: He lifts his eyes towards heaven and immediately lowers them.

shortDraft.en: He bows his head in thanksgiving.

guideDraft.en: He slightly bows his head during the words of thanksgiving.

shortDraft.en: Holding the Host in his left hand, he makes a cross over it with his right.

guideDraft.en: Holding the Host in his left hand, he makes a Sign of the Cross over it with his right.

shortDraft.en: He says fregit without breaking the Host.

guideDraft.en: He says the narrative words fregit, deditque without actually breaking the Host at that moment. The physical fraction belongs later in Mass.

shortDraft.en: He quietly pronounces the words of consecration.

guideDraft.en: Bending over the altar with elbows resting upon it, the priest pronounces the words of consecration of the Host distinctly, reverently and in a low voice.

shortDraft.en: He adores the consecrated Host with the first genuflection.

guideDraft.en: Immediately after the words of consecration he makes the first genuflection, in adoration.

shortDraft.en: He elevates the Host for the faithful to adore.

guideDraft.en: He rises and elevates the Host for the faithful to adore, keeping his eyes directed towards it; the elevation occurs after the first genuflection.

shortDraft.en: He replaces the Host, then genuflects.

guideDraft.en: The priest replaces the Host on the corporal and then makes his second genuflection.

shortDraft.en: He keeps his thumbs and index fingers joined, except to touch a consecrated Host, until the washing of his fingers.

guideDraft.en: From the Consecration onwards, his thumbs and index fingers remain joined except when he handles the consecrated Host, until the ablution of his fingers.

shortDraft.en: The server rings three times or continuously during the Host elevation.

guideDraft.en: During the elevation of the Host, the server rings the bell three times or continuously until the celebrant replaces the Host upon the corporal.

shortDraft.en: The chalice is uncovered, by the deacon when required at Solemn Mass; the priest raises it slightly.

guideDraft.en: After adoration of the Host, the chalice is uncovered, with form-dependent assistance of the deacon at Solemn Mass when required. At accipiens et hunc praeclarum Calicem the priest holds it near the knop with both hands, raises it slightly and immediately replaces it. This is not the major elevation.

shortDraft.en: At item tibi gratias agens, he bows his head.

guideDraft.en: At item tibi gratias agens he bows his head.

shortDraft.en: Holding the chalice in his left hand, he makes a cross over it with his right.

guideDraft.en: Holding the chalice in his left hand, he makes a Sign of the Cross over it with his right.

shortDraft.en: He holds the chalice with both hands.

guideDraft.en: He holds the chalice with both hands, left at the foot and right at the knop, preparing for the consecration.

shortDraft.en: Bending over the chalice, he quietly pronounces the words of the chalice consecration.

guideDraft.en: Bending towards the chalice, with his elbows resting upon the altar, the priest pronounces the words of consecration of the Precious Blood continuously, attentively and in a low voice.

shortDraft.en: He replaces the chalice, says Haec quotiescumque, then makes his first genuflection.

guideDraft.en: After the chalice consecration, the priest replaces the chalice, quietly says Hæc quotiescúmque and makes his first genuflection in adoration.

shortDraft.en: After the first genuflection, he elevates the chalice, replaces it, has it covered, then genuflects again.

guideDraft.en: After the first genuflection he rises and elevates the uncovered chalice for adoration. He replaces it; the chalice is covered according to the Mass form, with the deacon assisting at Solemn Mass when required; then he makes the second genuflection.

shortDraft.en: The server rings three times or continuously during the chalice elevation.

guideDraft.en: During the chalice elevation, the server rings three times or continuously until the chalice is placed back upon the corporal.

shortDraft.en: He resumes Unde et memores quietly, with hands extended.

guideDraft.en: After replacing and adoring the chalice he continues Unde et memores in a low voice, standing with hands extended.

shortDraft.en: At de tuis donis ac datis, he joins his hands.

guideDraft.en: At de tuis donis ac datis he joins his hands before his chest.

shortDraft.en: He makes three crosses over the Host and chalice.

guideDraft.en: He makes three successive Signs of the Cross over the Host and chalice together.

shortDraft.en: At Panem sanctum, he crosses the Host; at Calicem salutis, he crosses the chalice.

guideDraft.en: He signs over the Host only at Panem sanctum, and separately over the chalice at Calicem salutis.

shortDraft.en: At Supra quae, he keeps his hands extended.

guideDraft.en: The priest continues Supra quae standing with his hands extended before his chest.

shortDraft.en: At Supplices te rogamus, he bows at the centre of the altar with hands joined.

guideDraft.en: At Supplices te rogamus he bows at the centre of the altar, resting his joined hands upon it.

shortDraft.en: At ex hac altaris participatione, he kisses the altar.

guideDraft.en: At ex hac altaris participatione he kisses the altar, placing his hands on either side upon the corporal.

shortDraft.en: At Corpus, he crosses the Host; at Sanguinem, he crosses the chalice.

guideDraft.en: He makes a Sign of the Cross over the Host at Corpus, then separately over the chalice at Sanguinem.

shortDraft.en: At the cross after omni benedictione, he makes the Sign of the Cross upon himself.

guideDraft.en: At the cross following omni benedictione, he makes the Sign of the Cross upon himself from forehead to chest, keeping his left hand below his chest.

shortDraft.en: At Per eundem, he joins his hands.

guideDraft.en: At Per eundem he joins his hands.

shortDraft.en: At Memento etiam, he joins and raises his hands, looking towards the Blessed Sacrament.

guideDraft.en: At Memento etiam he joins and raises his hands before his face, looking towards the Blessed Sacrament on the altar.

shortDraft.en: He commemorates the faithful departed in a brief silence.

guideDraft.en: He commemorates the faithful departed according to his intention, as with the living.

shortDraft.en: He resumes with hands extended.

guideDraft.en: Once the commemoration ends, he resumes the prayer with hands extended.

shortDraft.en: At Per eundem, he joins his hands and bows his head.

guideDraft.en: At Per eundem he joins his hands and bows his head.

shortDraft.en: At Nobis quoque, he raises his voice and strikes his breast.

guideDraft.en: At Nobis quoque peccatoribus he raises his voice slightly and strikes his breast once with his right hand, his left resting on the corporal. The rest of the prayer is not said aloud.

shortDraft.en: At famulis tuis, he resumes the quiet voice with hands extended.

guideDraft.en: At famulis tuis his voice returns to the secret register and he continues with hands extended.

shortDraft.en: At Per Christum, he joins his hands.

guideDraft.en: At Per Christum he joins his hands.

shortDraft.en: At Per quem haec omnia, he keeps his hands joined.

guideDraft.en: At Per quem haec omnia he keeps his hands joined before his chest.

shortDraft.en: He makes three crosses over the Host and chalice.

guideDraft.en: He makes three successive Signs of the Cross over the Host and chalice together.

shortDraft.en: The chalice is uncovered, by the deacon at Solemn Mass when required; the priest genuflects and takes the Host.

guideDraft.en: At the conclusion of the Canon the chalice is uncovered by the celebrant at Low or Sung Mass, and by the deacon at Solemn Mass when required. The priest genuflects, rises and takes the Host between the thumb and index finger of his right hand.

shortDraft.en: At Per ipsum, cum ipso and in ipso, he makes three crosses with the Host over the chalice.

guideDraft.en: With the consecrated Host he makes three crosses over the chalice at Per ipsum, cum ipso and in ipso.

shortDraft.en: At Patri and Sancti, he makes two crosses with the Host between the chalice and his breast.

guideDraft.en: With the Host he makes two crosses between the chalice and his chest at Patri and Sancti.

shortDraft.en: He slightly raises the chalice, holding the Host above.

guideDraft.en: At omnis honor et gloria he holds the Host above the chalice with his right hand and slightly raises the chalice with the left, then replaces them. This minor elevation differs from the major elevations at the Consecration.

shortDraft.en: He replaces the sacred species; the chalice is covered, by the deacon at Solemn Mass when required; then the priest genuflects.

guideDraft.en: After the minor elevation the priest replaces the chalice and Host on the corporal. The chalice is covered with the pall; at Solemn Mass the deacon assists when required. The priest then genuflects.

shortDraft.en: He says Per omnia saecula saeculorum audibly.

guideDraft.en: After adoring the Sacrament he rises, extends his hands and places them on the altar on either side within the corporal, then says Per omnia saecula saeculorum audibly.

shortDraft.en: The respondent says Amen: the minister at Low Mass, or the appointed respondents at Sung Masses.

guideDraft.en: At the conclusion of the Canon, Per omnia saecula saeculorum is answered with Amen. At Low Mass the minister responds; in Sung Mass the appointed respondents give the answer.

shortDraft.en: The server gives the warning bell before consecration.

guideDraft.en: Shortly before the Consecration, the server rings a warning bell to alert the faithful.
